paper.title: Algorithm 794: Numerical Hankel transform by the Fortran program HANKEL
paper.venue: ACM TOMS 25(2), 240-250 (June 1999); the ACM article was not read (dl.acm.org refuses automated fetch from this host); the netlib archive was used

field: numerics (numerical Hankel transform of a test function with a closed-form transform)
stack: Fortran 77 (TOMS 794 netlib shell archive: Fortran77/Src/Dp/specfun.f and src.f, Fortran77/Drivers/Dp/driver.f)

claim.text: HT(XI=5.0, NU=1.0) printed by the authors' HANKEL driver into its result file, the shipped reference value 0.208245531E-01 (artifact-reference), absolute tolerance 1e-9 (fixed in the queue entry before any run).

reference.archive: netlib TOMS 794.gz, sha256 bdbd599bf88d0062a161aa01880b4a271a9fca31df3b13bd662c0ecfc83cab29, file Fortran77/Drivers/Dp/res (copied from the sandbox unpack)

attempt: The archive does not ship the machine constants D1MACH and I1MACH that specfun.f and src.f call (the PackingList names SrcLibs: port, which is absent). The original link fails on them (original-attempt-link.log, link_exit=1). We wrote impl/machine.f with IEEE double-precision values, from the PORT description, and linked it in with the authors' unmodified sources. No source file was edited, so the patch is build-only and proved by three manifests. Two builds (-O2 and -O0) give the same printed value, 0.208245531E-01, which matches the shipped reference.

original_attempt.tried: The authors' sources compiled and linked with gfortran 16.2.0 -O2 exactly as the archive's sources are, without machine.f
original_attempt.reason: link error: undefined reference to d1mach_ and i1mach_ from specfun.o and src.o (SrcLibs: port is not in the archive)

build_commands: gfortran -O2 driver.o src.o specfun.o machine.o -o hankel
